text:
marta: saw a new failure in staging where midstream eviction caused clients to lose the ability to resume. keeping state for every evicted stream is expensive. curious if we can do stateless resume tokens instead of server-side retention.

derek: interesting. you mean the gateway emits an opaque token the client can send back to continue? how do we avoid leaking model internal pointers?

marta: idea: token = base64( header.payload.signature ) where payload contains limited resume info: model-variant, sequence-offset, kv-digest (short), and a small fingerprint of prompt. sign with gateway key so we can validate without storing. no server-side per-stream retention.

ji-woo: pros: no KV retention, easier scaling. cons: token size grows, and sending internal kv-digest might be brittle if model checkpoint formats change. also potential security/privacy concerns.

marco: can we limit token contents to only offset + route + TTL and avoid kv details? handler could treat resume as a hint and re-run from last full checkpoint (e.g., every 256 tokens) rather than exact kv replay. cheaper but may re-compute some tokens.

derek: tradeoff: stateless resume increases compute on resume (replay) but reduces memory. billing implications: do we bill resumed tokens only once? likely we need to bill replayed tokens on retry.

marta: agreed. we should surface a trailer `x-rw-resume-token` and `x-rw-resume-ttl` when eviction is due. client shows "partial result (resume available)". retry sends `x-rw-resume:` header with token.

ji-woo: sketch of trailer: ```
Trailer:
  x-rw-resume-token: eyJhbGciOiJ...
  x-rw-resume-ttl: 60
  grpc-status: 8
```

marco: what about replay correctness? for stateless resume we may need a soft checkpointing policy in the model container: emit commit markers at boundaries so replay is deterministic from token offset.

derek: operationally, we need versioned token schemas. include a `v` field in token so older clients can still resume and gateway can interpret. key rotation plan also required.

marta: also consider an opt-in route flag `resume_mode: stateless|stateful|disabled`. default = stateless (cheap). customers that need exact byte-for-byte resume can opt into `stateful` which stores KV entries but costs more.

ji-woo: add metrics: `edge.resume.issued`, `edge.resume.used`, `edge.resume.failed` and a histogram for resume-latency. alert if resume-fail > 3% for 5m.

marco: tests: simulate random RST midstream, validate client gets token, then repost with token and check continuity within allowed drift. add fuzzing for rotated keys.

derek: privacy checklist: token must not contain PII or raw user data. only short fingerprint hash allowed. document that in RFC.

ops-bot: deploy planned: gateway/edge-proxy v1.43.0 -> canary us-east-1 :rocket:

marta: i'll draft RFC with token format, key rotation, opt-in route config, and billing implications. link when ready.

ops-bot: deploy success: gateway/edge-proxy v1.43.0 canary -> 2/3 hosts (us-east-1) succeeded.
